title: Prevalence and Systemic Factors Associated with Periodontitis among Kidney Transplant Recipients: A Cross-sectional Study in Vietnam.
abstract: Kidney transplant recipients (KTRs) are particularly vulnerable to periodontal disease due to long-term immunosuppression, metabolic disturbances, and chronic inflammation. However, data in Southeast Asia remain scarce. The aim of the study was to determine the prevalence, stage distribution of periodontitis, and to examine systemic and behavioral factors associated with the disease among Vietnamese KTRs; as a secondary exploratory aim, we evaluated selected systemic biomarkers (C-reactive protein [CRP], serum urea, and platelet count [PLT]) and descriptively summarized their cross-sectional discrimination with respect to the periodontitis status using prespecified receiver operating characteristic (ROC) analyses. A cross-sectional analytical study among 300 KTRs at 103 Military Hospital, Vietnam Military University, Hanoi, Vietnam. A cross-sectional study was conducted among 300 KTRs at a teaching hospital in Hanoi, Vietnam, from June 2025 to October 2025. Periodontitis was defined and staged according to the 2017 World Workshop on the Classification of Periodontal and Peri-Implant Diseases and Conditions (American Academy of Periodontology/European Federation of Periodontology). Descriptive statistics, chi-square/Fisher's exact test, and logistic regression were used to examine associations. Crude and adjusted odds ratios (ORs and aORs) were calculated. An exploratory ROC analysis was performed to assess the discriminatory ability of selected clinical and biochemical variables. Chi-square, t test, analysis of variance, multivariate logistic regression, and ROC analysis using Statistical Package for the Social Sciences version 27.0 were used for statistical analyses. Periodontitis was present in 77.7% of participants. Stage I disease was most prevalent (33.0%), followed by Stage II (27.0%) and Stage III (16.3%); only 1.3% of patients had Stage IV disease. In multivariable analysis, poor oral hygiene (OHI-S; aOR = 3.47), lower PLTs (aOR = 0.986), higher CRP levels (CRP; aOR = 1.32), and elevated serum urea (aOR = 2.09) were independently associated with periodontitis. Periodontitis is highly prevalent in Vietnamese KTRs, predominantly in moderate stages, underscoring the need for preventive strategies. Systemic inflammation, renal biomarkers, and poor oral hygiene were strongly associated with disease. Integrating periodontal assessment into routine post-transplant care may support preventive oral health strategies in this population.

title: Application of computational methods in the drug discovery and development of Alzheimer's disease.
abstract: Alzheimer's disease (AD) is a prevalent neurodegenerative disorder marked by the accumulation of amyloid plaques and neurofibrillary tangles in the brain, leading to cognitive decline. As the most common dementia, AD affects over 50 million individuals worldwide, with 10 million new cases each year. Despite many significant progresses in AD research fields, there is still no effective treatment. Advances in molecular modelling and artificial intelligence (AI) algorithm have facilitated the application of computational methods in AD drug development, offering advantages in terms of efficiency, cost-effectiveness, and resource conservation. These strategies, including molecular docking, molecular dynamics simulation, protein structure prediction, virtual screening, and de novo drug design, have been widely employed in the past decades. Additionally, AI pharmaceutical companies have revolutionized the traditional drug development pipeline such as AD biomarker discovery, accurate diagnosis and precision medicine, etc. This review offers a thorough summary of recent progresses in computational-based methodologies in the study of AD drug development, including the elucidation the pathological mechanism at the molecular level, target identification, target 3D structure prediction, lead compound discovery, de novo molecular generation, multi-target directed ligands, drug repurposing, biomarker discovery, etc., showing promising applications of molecular modelling and AI in the development of AD therapy.

title: Gapless Complete Genome and Multi-Omics Illuminate Immune Adaptation and Host-Virus Interactions in a Coronavirus Reservoir.
abstract: Bats are major reservoirs of emerging viruses, including severe acute respiratory syndrome-related coronaviruses, yet they exhibit remarkable tolerance to viral infections with limited clinical manifestations-a longstanding immunological paradox. Here, we generate a telomere-to-telomere (T2T) de novo genome assembly for Rhinolophus sinicus (R. sinicus), designated T2T-RSC1.0 (2.14 Gb), comprising 17 fully anchored autosomes and both sex chromosomes. This gapless assembly resolves 129.19 Mb of previously unresolved regions (PURs) and enables annotation of 848 previously unannotated genes, including 131 protein-coding genes and five pseudogenes on the 33.75 Mb Y chromosome. Using 2.12 × 10<sup>5</sup> newly identified single-nucleotide polymorphisms within PURs, population genomic analyses resolve three major genetic groups and provide improved resolution of genome-wide population structure. Comparative analyses further reveal population-level associations between major histocompatibility complex polymorphism and viral diversity. Multi-omics and functional analyses reveal a coordinated evolutionary remodeling of antiviral defense, antigen presentation, cytokine signaling, and inflammatory regulation in horseshoe bats. This study provides an unparalleled genomic resource for R. sinicus and establishes an integrated framework for investigating immune evolution, long-term host-virus coexistence, and mammalian adaptive evolution.

title: Efficacy of Mat Pilates on the resting blood pressure and health related quality of life in individuals with systemic hypertension versus standard care: study protocol for a single centered single blinded randomized controlled trial.
abstract: Systemic hypertension is a global non-communicable disease that creates an essential need for alternate forms of lifestyle modifications, including exercise, to lower elevated blood pressure. Mat Pilates, a feasible form of mind-body coordinated exercise, may provide benefits with limited resources. This randomized controlled trial aims to assess the efficacy of Mat Pilates on resting blood pressure and health-related quality of life in individuals with systemic hypertension. A two-arm, single-blinded, block randomized controlled trial will be recruited with a total of 120 participants into control and experimental groups 60 participants in each group (1:1 ratio). Mat Pilates will be administered to the experimental group and standard care to the control group for 12 weeks. Resting and central blood pressure, health-related quality of life, and echocardiographic parameters will be measured before and after the trial. We hypothesized that Pilates may not be beneficial in lowering resting blood pressure in hypertensive patients. A repeated-measures analysis of variance (ANOVA) will test the within- and between-group effects of Mat Pilates on various outcomes. The trial was approved by the Institutional Research Committee, Manipal College of Health Professions, Manipal Academy of Higher Education, Kasturba Medical College, and Kasturba Hospital Institutional Ethics Committee, Manipal. Written informed consent will be obtained from all the participants. All stakeholders and committees will communicate key findings regarding the implementation of mind-body association exercises as a measure of lifestyle modification in individuals with systemic hypertension. Clinical Trials Registry of India: CTRI/2021/07/035002. Registered on July 20, 2021, http://ctri.nic.in.

title: Incidence and Associated Risk Factors of Coeliac Disease in Children Newly Diagnosed With Type 1 Diabetes: A 5-Year Nationwide Prospective Study From Kuwait.
abstract: Kuwait has one of the highest global incidences of childhood type 1 diabetes (T1D), yet little is known about the burden of coeliac disease (CD) in this population. We aimed to determine the prevalence/incidence of CD in children newly diagnosed with T1D in Kuwait and identify associated risk factors. In this prospective cohort study, all 1938 children (≤ 14 years) diagnosed with T1D in Kuwait between 2011 and 2017 were enrolled and followed for 5 years post-diagnosis. CD development was defined by intestinal biopsy confirmation. Cox univariable regression models quantified associations between several characteristics at T1D diagnosis (age, sex, DKA, height z-score and BMI z-score) and incident CD risk. Four baseline CD cases were excluded. Of the remaining 1934 children, 65 (3.4%) developed CD during follow-up. The median time to CD diagnosis was 1.5 years; 40% were diagnosed within the first year. The incidence rate within the first year following T1D diagnosis was 1.35 (95% CI 0.92-1.99) per 100 person-years and generally declined over subsequent years of follow-up. While age at diagnosis showed no clear effect shortly after T1D diagnosis, older age was associated with progressively lower CD risk over longer follow-up, with the risk of CD being 33% lower per one-year increase in age at diagnosis by 5 years of follow-up; no other baseline factors investigated were significant. This nationwide prospective study highlights the burden and timing of biopsy-confirmed CD after T1D onset. CD occurred most frequently during the early years after T1D diagnosis, with a higher risk among younger children, supporting particular attention to screening in these groups.

title: Oral Adverse Effects of Semaglutide Therapy: A Narrative Review.
abstract: Semaglutide, a glucagon-like peptide-1-receptor agonist, is widely used for the management of type-2 diabetes mellitus and obesity. Despite its increasing clinical use, the drug's oral adverse effect profile remains inadequately characterized. This narrative review aimed to analyze the current evidence on semaglutide-associated oral adverse effects, with emphasis on mechanistic pathways, integration of pharmacovigilance and clinical data, and emerging implications for oral health and dental practice. A comprehensive literature search was conducted across PubMed, Scopus, ScienceDirect, Web of Science, and Google Scholar. Keywords related to semaglutide and oral adverse effects were used. Eligible studies included clinical trials, pharmacovigilance analyses, observational studies, case reports, and preclinical research reporting oral adverse effects or relevant mechanistic insights. Studies lacking oral health correlates were excluded. Findings were narratively reviewed in accordance with Scale for the Assessment of Narrative Review Articles guidelines. Xerostomia or hyposalivation is the most consistently reported oral adverse effect, although its prevalence varies across studies. However, xerostomia often occurs secondarily to gastrointestinal symptoms including nausea, reduced oral intake, and delayed gastric emptying. Additional manifestations included dysgeusia, dry throat, oral paresthesia or hypoesthesia, halitosis, frothy saliva, and increased dental caries. Pharmacovigilance data show significant signals for dry mouth and altered taste. Case-series confirm semaglutide-associated hyposalivation. Limited evidence suggests increased susceptibility to oral candidiasis. Early experimental and observational data indicate potential modulatory effects on inflammation, tissue repair, and bone metabolism. Semaglutide therapy is associated with oral adverse effects, mainly xerostomia and sensory disturbances, which may compromise oral health. Awareness of these outcomes highlights the need for interdisciplinary oral health monitoring.

title: Patterns of irrational drug use in pediatric acute respiratory infections: A hospital- based cross- sectional study in South India.
abstract: Irrational drug use is a growing public health concern, with the World Health Organization estimating that 50% of prescriptions worldwide are irrational. Data on rational drug prescriptions for acute respiratory infections (ARIs) in children are limited. Children under 14 years of age with ARIs visiting a tertiary care hospital in South India were enrolled. Data on prescriptions, demographics, and clinical information were collected and analyzed. A total of 156 children (median age: 2 years, 53.8% male) were enrolled. The most common ARI was upper respiratory tract infection (65.3%), followed by viral bronchiolitis/pneumonia (22.3%). Of 262 prescriptions, 86.2% were written by physicians, and 13.7% were self-prescribed. The median number of drugs per child was 3 (range: 2-5). Antibiotics were included in 58.8% of physician prescriptions (97.7% irrational), and 61.9% included cough medications (65.7% irrational). A viral pathogen was detected in 35% of children who received antibiotics. Commonly prescribed antibiotics were cephalosporins and amoxicillin-clavulanate, while cough syrups included chlorpheniramine-phenylephrine, levosalbutamol, ambroxol, and guaifenesin. Only 12.3% of prescriptions used generic drug names, and polypharmacy (≥2 medications) was found in 81.4% of prescriptions. Presence of sore throat and respiratory distress were associated with antibiotic prescription by physicians. This study highlights a high prevalence of irrational drug use in children with ARIs, with inappropriate antibiotic and cough medication prescriptions. There is a need for better prescribing practices, diagnostic accuracy, and adherence to evidence-based guidelines.

title: An open-label, Phase 1 study to evaluate the drug-drug interaction between ulonivirine and the combined oral contraceptive levonorgestrel/ethinyl estradiol in female participants without HIV with a validated liquid chromatograph.
abstract: Ulonivirine is a non-nucleoside reverse transcriptase inhibitor in development as an oral, once-weekly treatment for HIV-1 in combination with investigational islatravir. The effect of ulonivirine on the pharmacokinetics of an oral contraceptive, levonorgestrel (LNG)/ethinyl estradiol (EE) was evaluated in females without HIV. In this Phase 1 study (MK-8507-009), postmenopausal or oophorectomized females received a single dose of LNG/EE (0.1 mg/0.02 mg), followed by a 5-day washout period. Participants then received ulonivirine 400 mg once-weekly for 3 weeks, and LNG/EE was co-administered with the third dose. Blood samples were collected for pharmacokinetics analysis. Safety and tolerability were monitored by clinical and laboratory assessments. Twenty adults (90% White; 100% Hispanic or Latina) were enrolled (median age, 56 years; range, 47-66 years). Two participants discontinued for reasons considered unrelated to ulonivirine. The geometric mean ratios ([LNG/EE + ulonivirine]/[LNG/EE]; 90% CI) for plasma AUC<sub>0-inf</sub> of LNG and EE were 0.88 (0.84-0.93) and 0.85 (0.82-0.89). Maximum plasma concentration of LNG and EE decreased (26% and 20%, respectively) with LNG/EE + ulonivirine versus LNG/EE alone. Ulonivirine pharmacokinetics were similar for LNG/EE + ulonivirine and LNG/EE alone. Four participants (20%) experienced ≥1 adverse event: 2 (10%) after administration of LNG/EE alone and 2 (10.5%) after co-administration of LNG/EE + ulonivirine. All adverse events were mild and considered unrelated to study intervention. Co-administration of ulonivirine 400 mg once-weekly with a single dose of LNG/EE had no clinically meaningful effect on the pharmacokinetics of LNG or EE in females without HIV and was generally well tolerated.

title: Neural Cell Adhesion Molecule-1 Gene Polymorphism Increases the Risk of Cognitive Dysfunction in Schizophrenia Spectrum Disorder.
abstract: Neural cell adhesion molecule-1 (NCAM-1), a marker of synaptic plasticity is reported to be altered and associated with cognitive dysfunction in schizophrenia. The aim of the study was to analyse the allele and genotype frequency of neural cell adhesion molecule-1 (NCAM-I) gene polymorphism (rs1836796, rs2303377, rs584427, rs646558) and plasma NCAM-I levels in schizophrenia and their association with cognitive function. Two hundred and sixteen (216) schizophrenia patients and 216 controls were enrolled in the study. NCAM-I polymorphism and its plasma levels were analysed in cases and controls. Cognitive status was evaluated using ACE-III scores. The rs 1836796 genotype was associated with cognitive status (p = 0.011) in schizophrenia. Among the genotypes of rs 1836796, the TT variant (OR: 2.193, 95% CI: 1.097-4.386, p = 0.0292) conferred a potential increased risk of schizophrenia. Attention score (p < 0.05), memory score (p < 0.01), fluency score (p < 0.01), language score (p < 0.01), Visuospatial abilities score (p < 0.01) and total ACE III scores (p < 0.01) were significantly reduced; negative symptom score (p < 0.01), general psychopathological Score (p < 0.01) and total PANSS score (p < 0.01) was significantly increased in TT genotype compared to GG genotype. We conclude that single nucleotide polymorphisms of NCAM-I increase the risk of schizophrenia and are related to severity of the disease and cognitive impairment. The online version contains supplementary material available at https://doi.org/10.1007/s12291-024-01290-0.

title: Whole genome sequencing approach for the detection of rare protein-altering variants associated with familial male infertility.
abstract: Whole-genome sequencing (WGS) is an efficient, accurate, and high-throughput technique used for the discovery of exonic as well as non-exonic variants causing different genetic anomalies, improving clinical management for the disease. This study was designed to evaluate pathogenic genetic variants related to male infertility in male infertile families in remote rural areas of Pakistan. For the five families recruited, WGS was conducted on 14 patients and 6healthy controls. WGS was performed using the Illumina TruSeq DNA Nano Library Prep workflow protocol. DNA was assessed with TapeStation and sequenced using the TruSeq kit (Illumina). Bioinformatics tools were then used to identify potential causative variants, including indels and single-nucleotide variants. In family 1, five homozygous nonsynonymous SNVs were identified in FMR1, PHF8, TOPBP1, and DAB2IP. These X-linked or recessive variants cause amino acid changes that affect key cellular pathways. In family 10, homozygous nonsynonymous SNVs were detected in FOS, MIR452, PDHA1, and SERPINB1, implicating roles in structural, transcriptional, metabolic, and synaptic processes. In family 11, a frameshift deletion in PRDM9 and nonsynonymous SNVs in KIAA1210, suggesting possible disruption of gene regulation and protein stability. In family 13, multiple nonsynonymous variants were identified in SPATA20, and G6PD,, with implications in reproductive function, angiogenesis, enzymatic activity, and neuromuscular disorders. SNV Variant was detected in SLC12A4 in Family 15. The study contributes to a systematic understanding of the problem and provides a basis for identifying causal variations in idiopathic cases of male infertility, setting targets for future therapeutic development.

title: A Bi-Adjuvant Senolytic Nanovaccine Modulating Dendritic Cell Senescence Ameliorates Aging-Related Metabolic Dysfunction.
abstract: Senolytic vaccines hold promise for eliminating senescent cells, but their efficacy is limited by poor seno-antigen immunogenicity and age-related dendritic cell (DC) dysfunction. Here, we engineered an active biomaterial-enabled bi-adjuvant senolytic nanovaccine (CK5-GC-NV) by co-assembling CpG oligodeoxynucleotide with a fusion protein of the seno-antigen Gpnmb and a cationic spider silk protein variant (CK5). Beyond antigen delivery, the CK5 scaffold acts as an intrinsic senomodulator associated with the downregulation of mitotic kinases Aurka/b and a concomitant decrease in senescence-associated PI3K/AKT phosphorylation in DCs. This intervention attenuates aged DC phenotypes, restores antigen cross-presentation, and synergizes with CpG to elicit potent cytotoxic T-lymphocyte responses against senescent targets. Across multiple aging mouse models, CK5-GC-NV immunization orchestrated targeted clearance of Gpnmb<sup>+</sup> senescent adipocytes, profoundly ameliorating metabolic dysfunction and extending lifespan. This multifunctional biomaterial platform integrates seno-antigen immunogenicity enhancement with the restoration of aged DC function, providing a promising proof-of-concept for antigen-directed gerotherapeutics.

title: The Trouble with "Cure" in Sickle Cell Gene Therapy.
abstract: This letter responds to the essay "Transformed but Not Cured: The Ethics of Describing Gene-Editing Therapy for Sickle Cell Disease," by Jada Wiggleton-Little, Shameka Poetry Thomas, Kristin Walters, and Consuela Albright, in the May-June 2026 issue of the Hastings Center Report.

title: Investigation of Association of TYK2-P1104A Variant in Systemic Lupus Erythematosus Patients With or Without Tuberculosis.
abstract: Systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE) is a complex disorder involving a hyperactive immune system. SLE is debilitating, with limited options for treatment. Recent advances in understanding the disease, its etiology, and genetics have made management more efficient. There has been a paradigm shift in the treatment over the past few decades from symptomatic management to the recent exciting reports of drug-free remission. Thus, detecting factors contributing to or protecting against the disease is paramount for better-personalized medicine. Additionally, infections due to SLE account for a majority of morbidity and mortality. Tuberculosis (TB) is one of the prevalent chronic infections that affect SLE patients, although the prevalence as well as mortality is high in countries in which TB is endemic. TYK2 (non-receptor tyrosine-protein kinase) is essential in generating immune responses by developing pro-inflammatory cytokines. P1104A mutation in TYK2 is a missense mutation and impairs the normal functioning of TYK2, in turn impairing the production/action of pro-inflammatory cytokines. TYK2-P1104A is beneficial in SLE patients and has a protective effect. However, due to impaired generation of cytokines and diminished response against TB, the possibility of TYK2-P1104A mutation in TB patients is high. The literature also points to the fact that the frequency of this allele is low in different populations, and the data related to its clinical effects is limited. Our study found no TYK2-P1104A allele in SLE patients, SLE patients who have TB, and TB patients, as well as healthy controls.

title: Neonatal-onset developmental and epileptic encephalopathy: High genetic yield and long-term outcomes in a multicenter southern European cohort.
abstract: To determine the genetic diagnostic yield, characterize the clinical and genetic landscape, and evaluate long-term epilepsy, neurodevelopmental, and survival outcomes in a strictly defined cohort of neonatal-onset developmental and epileptic encephalopathy (DEE). Retrospective multicenter observational study across tertiary epilepsy centers in Italy, Greece, and Spain. Sixty-two full-term neonates fulfilling ILAE 2022 criteria for DEE with seizure onset within the first 30 days of life and a minimum follow-up of 18 months were included. All patients underwent next-generation sequencing-based genetic testing. Genetic findings, clinical characteristics, and long-term outcomes were systematically analyzed. A molecular diagnosis was established in 82.2% of patients (51/62), identifying variants across 29 genes grouped, for descriptive purposes, into four broad categories according to principal biological role. First-line whole-exome sequencing achieved higher diagnostic yield than targeted gene panels (88.9% vs. 41.2%), although this comparison was influenced by differences in testing era and strategy. KCNQ2 variants were the most frequent genetic cause (29.4%), and several treatable metabolic disorders were identified. After a mean follow-up of 11.9 years, 64.5% of patients had drug-resistant epilepsy and mortality reached 17.7%. Seizure freedom was achieved in a subset of patients, particularly those with KCNQ2-related DEE. Nevertheless, severe-to-profound intellectual disability affected 71.7% of evaluable patients and persisted even among those who became seizure-free, suggesting that neurodevelopmental outcomes are influenced by factors beyond seizure burden, including the underlying genetic disorder and other disease-related factors. However, the marked variability observed precludes any causal inference from these data. This large European cohort demonstrates a high genetic diagnostic yield in neonatal-onset DEE, supporting first-line whole-exome sequencing as the preferred first-tier genetic test. The persistence of severe neurodevelopmental impairment despite seizure control highlights the need for precision therapies targeting disease mechanisms in addition to seizure management. We studied 62 newborns who developed severe epilepsy caused by genetic changes, following them for up to 25 years. We found a genetic cause in over 80% of cases, and genetic testing that reads the entire genetic code was far more effective than tests that only look at specific genes. Although seizures improved in some children over time, nearly all had lasting intellectual disability regardless of seizure control. This suggests that the underlying genetic condition may contribute substantially to brain development in addition to the effects of seizures, although our study cannot determine the relative contribution of each factor.

title: Rationally Designed Zwitterionic Peptides Improve siRNA Delivery of Cationic Diblock Copolymer-Based Nanoparticle Drug-Delivery Systems.
abstract: Nanoparticle drug delivery systems (NP DDS) have proven to be tremendously impactful for delivering therapeutic agents in cancer treatments, vaccinations, gene therapy, diagnostics, and enabled new agents such as RNA therapeutics. However, the exposure of NP DDS to biological milieus leads to the rapid adsorption of proteins and other molecules, forming a proteinaceous corona that obscures NP surface characteristics and controls the biological interactions of the NP DDS. This corona often potentiates phagocytic uptake, hindering the efficacy of targeting groups, and reducing NP drug delivery efficacy. Surface modifications to reduce protein adsorption can overcome these deleterious effects. Still, the repertoire of modifications is limited to poly(ethylene glycol) (PEG)and synthetic zwitterionic polymers. However, these anti-fouling strategies lack tunability, have off-target immunological effects, and suffer from targeting-limited steric hindrance, altogether motivating the development of alternative approaches. Peptides can uniquely form many zwitterions and have shown promise in reducing and controlling NP protein coronas as a function of peptide sequence. However, the impact of ZIPs on the drug delivery properties of polymeric NPs has not been explored. In this work, diverse zwitterionic peptides (ZIPs) predicted computationally to reduce protein adsorption by assessing peptide-peptide β-strand interaction energies were conjugated to pH-responsive cationic NPs. The resulting ZIP-NP conjugates exhibited up to 88% reduced protein adsorption versus unfunctionalized NP, resulting in a range of siRNA-mediated gene knockdown, outcomes that correlate with interaction energies. These data suggest that interaction energy is a promising design parameter for ZIPs. ZIP-NP also exhibited sequence-dependent variations in cellular uptake and circulation half-life, indicating ZIP-NPs are suitable for tuning and improving NP drug delivery characteristics.

title: Computational analysis of treatment resistant cancer cells.
abstract: Prostate cancer (PC), which is a disease driven by the activity of the androgen receptor (AR), is the most commonly diagnosed malignancy and despite advances in diagnostic and treatment strategies, PC is the second most common cause of cancer mortality in men. Taxane-based chemotherapy is the only chemotherapy that prolongs survival in metastatic PC patients. At the cellular level, taxanes bind to and stabilize microtubules (MTs), inhibiting all MT-dependent intracellular pathways. MTs are highly dynamic polymers that stochastically switch between phases of growth, shrinkage, and pause. Altered MT dynamics endow cancer cells with both survival and migratory advantages. Taxanes inhibit MT dynamics and alter the spatial organization of the MT network, thereby inhibiting intracellular trafficking of molecular cargo critical for tumor survival. In PC specifically, taxanes inhibit transcriptional activity downstream of MT stabilization and AR nuclear accumulation. Different tubulin inhibitors, even from within the same structural class as the taxanes, affect distinct parameters of MT dynamics, yet the selection of taxane for chemotherapy is not based on the particular patterns of dynamic behavior of the MT cytoskeleton in individual patients. We envisage that systematic characterization using quantitative analysis of MT dynamics in PC patient cells expressing clinically relevant protein isoforms, before and after treatment with each of the taxanes, will allow us to identify criteria for the selection of the most suitable drug combination at the onset of treatment. We link MT dynamics in the presence of AR variants and sensitivity/resistance to taxanes and connect fundamental research with clinically relevant concepts to elucidate cellular mechanisms of clinical response to taxanes and, thus, advance the customization of therapy. Our computational live-cell analysis addresses questions in the context of the inherent differences in MT homeostasis as a function of AR content in PC cells, the specific parameters of MT dynamics each of the taxanes affects, and how this information can be used to match endogenous patterns of MT dynamics with drug-modulated MT behavior. We investigate whether the sensitivity to taxanes, evaluated by computational analysis of MTs, can be linked to gene expression of the AR and its variants, whether the resistance to taxanes can be linked to the presence of a specific AR splice variant, and whether we can identify which of the taxanes will be most effective based on the endogenous patterns of MT dynamics.

title: Modifiable adiposity-related risk for chronic kidney disease in APOL1 variant carriers: Pilot study results.
abstract: Background: Apolipoprotein L1 (APOL1) genetic variants are associated with the development of chronic kidney disease (CKD), but disease expression appears to depend on metabolic and environmental modifiers. Obesity is a risk factor for several chronic diseases. However, the relationship between obesity, body fat, and the development of kidney disease mediated by APOL1 risk variants is unknown. Aim: This study examined relationships among APOL1 risk variants, nutritional status, with a focus on anthropometry and body composition, and selected renal function biomarkers in individuals with CKD. Methods: Adults with CKD were genotyped for APOL1 variants, resulting in APOL1 risk and APOL1 non-risk groups. Results: The APOL1 risk group showed higher body mass index, increased central abdominal fat, and greater body fat compared with established reference values (p < 0.05). This group also showed high serum creatinine levels and a low estimated glomerular filtration rate, both abnormal ranges (p < 0.05). Conclusions: These findings demonstrate excessive body and abdominal fat as a relevant target for precision nutrition strategies to reduce CKD risk and support management in APOL1-associated kidney disease. Also, it is necessary to identify carriers before the onset of CKD and to use medical nutrition therapy to prevent or delay disease progression.
